bullets.text: Avendus Spark initiates VAML at BUY, TP Rs525 (6x FY28 EV/EBITDA), sees FY28E EBITDA Rs406bn vs Rs255bn in FY26.
bullets.source: Avendus Spark - Initiating coverage on Vedanta Aluminium (BUY, TP: Rs.525)

detail.summary: Avendus argues VAML's Balco ramp-up and backward integration into alumina, bauxite and coal cut reliance on LME gains for growth, with the target price embedding a conservative $2,750/t FY28 LME versus its own $3,000/t house view.
points: FY27/28E EBITDA Rs386bn/Rs406bn vs Rs255bn FY26
Growth projects add ~Rs100bn EBITDA potential (40% of FY26)
Consol net debt to ~$1bn FY28 vs $3.1bn Q1FY27

bullets.text: CLSA maintains O-PF on Hindalco, TP Rs1,240; management guides EBITDA to more than double by FY32 off FY26 levels.
bullets.source: CLSA - Hindalco (HNDL IB): IF26 takeaways

detail.summary: CLSA's IF26 takeaways tie the doubling guide to Novelis' Bay Minette ramp and Oswego's tariff relief, India upstream capacity nearly doubling with captive coal cutting costs, and India downstream scaling five-fold, while consol leverage stays contained as Novelis debt peaks.
points: India upstream capacity to 2.4mt from 1.3mt currently
Captive coal mines cut cost $200/t vs FY24 levels
India downstream EBITDA to $1bn from $200m currently
Novelis net debt peaks 4QFY27 despite $10bn India capex

bullets.text: Vedanta Aluminium ranks 2nd among India's SEZ goods exporters at $3.5bn exports; Zambian copper smelter also resumed operations.
bullets.source: Kotak - Basic materials - daily news and prices

detail.summary: Kotak's daily wrap flags two dated Vedanta items alongside broader sector headlines: the SEZ export ranking and the Zambian copper smelter restarting after scheduled maintenance.
points: Vedanta Aluminium: $3.5bn SEZ exports, ranks #2 nationally
Zambian copper smelter resumed after maintenance shutdown
Core sector output +4.8% YoY in August 2026

bullets.text: India rebar +4% WoW/+13% MoM, HRC +3% WoW/+9% MoM; domestic HRC now at parity with China post safeguard duty.
bullets.source: UBS India Sales - Steel Price Rally (India Metals & Mining Weekly)

detail.summary: UBS frames continued India steel strength as domestic pricing catching up with China after safeguard duties, even as China's own rebar/HRC and coking-coal complex eased on supply directives and base metals softened on the same read.
points: India HRC +3% WoW / +9% MoM, now at China parity

bullets.text: JSW Steel and JSW Energy plan $300mn debt sales, per Reuters coverage in Kotak's daily wrap.
bullets.source: Kotak - Basic materials - daily news and prices

detail.summary: Kotak's aggregator flags JSW Group's planned $300m debt raise across JSW Steel and JSW Energy, alongside a separate Reuters item that BigMint's India steel index hit a 4-year high on strong demand and falling inventories.
points: $300mn debt sales planned across JSW Steel + JSW Energy
BigMint India steel index at 4-year high
Core sector output +4.8% YoY in August 2026

bullets.text: MS keeps UTCEM as sole cement OW; Shree, Dalmia, ACC UW, ACEM EW, flagging cement stocks already down ~14% YTD.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - MS India Trends & Themes: Coal India upgraded to OW; India Cement Faces Renewed Cost Inflation Risks

detail.summary: MS frames cement as a 'worth flagging' story alongside the Coal India upgrade, keeping only UltraTech at OW while Ambuja stays EW and Shree, Dalmia and ACC remain UW, as cost inflation threatens FY27 estimates without adequate pricing action.
points: Pricing needed to protect FY27 ests

bullets.text: Cement demand holds at 7-8% YoY with stable pan-India trade prices, but MS still expects near-term earnings pressure without pricing action.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - [MS] India Materials | CIL u/g to OW; Cement cost pressures back in focus

detail.summary: MS argues petcoke and thermal coal, both up ~20% since July-end, are shifting from a one-quarter buffer to a higher-for-longer cost cycle, with inventory and domestic-coal switching only delaying rather than eliminating the hit into 3QFY27.

bullets.text: ~15% below-normal monsoon is a later, rural-demand risk for cement — MS pegs the hit to 4QFY27/1QFY28, not this quarter.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - [MS] India Materials | CIL u/g to OW; Cement cost pressures back in focus

detail.summary: MS separates the monsoon call from the near-term cost story: the ~15% rainfall deficit reaches rural cement demand only with a lag via agricultural income, pushing the impact into 4QFY27/1QFY28.
points: Lag: rainfall -> agri income -> rural demand

bullets.text: E-auction premiums jumped to 59% in Aug from 41% in Jul; MS says every 10ppt further gain adds ~6% to CIL's EPS.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - [MS] India Materials | CIL u/g to OW; Cement cost pressures back in focus

detail.summary: MS's Coal India upgrade to OW rests heavily on the e-auction premium trajectory, which rose sharply in a single month, directly lifting realisations and driving the ~20% FY27 EPS upgrade.

bullets.text: Thermal power demand accelerated to ~20% YoY in Sep MTD vs ~12% in Aug, with plant inventories at a 5-yr low of ~7 days.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - [MS] India Materials | CIL u/g to OW; Cement cost pressures back in focus

detail.summary: The volume case behind the CIL upgrade is a restocking story: dispatches track thermal demand closely, and plant coal stocks have fallen to their lowest in five years, setting up a replenishment tailwind on top of accelerating demand.
points: Sep MTD thermal power demand +~20% YoY
Plant inventories ~7 days vs ~19 in Mar

bullets.text: MS flags downside risks to the CIL call: weaker e-auction premiums, crude-led cost pressure and wage hikes assumed in the FY27 upgrade.
bullets.source: Morgan Stanley - MS India Trends & Themes: Coal India upgraded to OW; India Cement Faces Renewed Cost Inflation Risks

detail.summary: MS frames the CIL call as an earnings upgrade rather than a re-rating, trading near its long-term average multiple, and lists three swing factors that could unwind the thesis.
points: Valuation ~6.6x fwd P/E, near LT avg

bullets.text: Dixon Chairman targets top-10 global EMS in 5 years, top-5 in 10, scaling mobile volumes 40mn to 65mn via Vivo JV; ROCEs held above 30%.
bullets.source: JPM - Dixon Technologies: Chairman spotlight at JPM India Conference: Exports to drive next leg of growth

detail.summary: Chairman Vachani frames exports, not domestic demand, as the next EMS growth leg, with India's electronics exports targeted from $40bn to $150bn by 2030. Component manufacturing (camera/display modules) is meant to lift mobile value-addition without diluting the 30%+ ROCE, aided by ECMS.
points: 40mn to 65mn mobile units via Vivo JV
30%+ ROCE floor kept on new investment
Also eyeing defense, medical, drones via M&A

bullets.text: Kaynes FY26 operating cash flow swung to -Rs6.0bn (FY25: -Rs0.8bn) as receivable days doubled to 154, cash conversion cycle hit 226 days.
bullets.source: Kotak - Mankind - UPGD BUY; Kaynes - More of the same; INDO MIM - Initiate; Curious Case of ONGC vs OINL

detail.summary: Kaynes' 33.2% FY26 revenue growth leans increasingly on the captive GridCrest/KEMS smart-metering business while core EMS ex-smart-meters grew just 3%, and cash generation has deteriorated sharply alongside a receivables build.
points: Revenue +33.2% YoY, core EMS ex-meters only +3%
GridCrest/KEMS smart metering ~43% of FY26 EBITDA
Receivable days doubled to 154, CCC 226 days
FCF outflow -Rs18.5bn after capex and acquisitions

bullets.text: Voltas RAC secondary sales +15-20% YoY, share 18.6% vs #2's 12%; read-through for Amber/PGEL AC components.
bullets.source: Emkay - Voltas: Prioritizing market share over near-term margins; BUY; Target: Rs1,500 (+3 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Voltas management is explicitly prioritizing market share and absolute EBIT over near-term margin recovery; 2QFY27 RAC demand benefits from a weak GST-disruption base and healthy channel inventory, with price hikes only partly offsetting commodity/BEE-driven cost increases.
points: Cumulative price hikes ~10-12% vs ~8% GST benefit
Channel inventory <30 days across the industry

bullets.text: CLSA: HLD on TCS/Infosys/HCLTech, U-PF on Wipro; sees most EPS downside risk in Infosys and Wipro as 2Q27 demand stays cautious.
bullets.source: CLSA - CLSA India Research - LG Electronics | Juniper Hotels | India IT

detail.summary: CLSA's 2Q27 India IT preview finds demand commentary cautious across the board as macro, geopolitics, rates and inflation mute discretionary spend. HCL's tone is the most resilient; order books and headcounts look broadly stable, and BFSI remains a relative bright spot.
points: 2Q27 demand commentary cautious across TCS, Infosys, Wipro, HCL
HCL's demand commentary the most resilient of the four
BFSI resilient despite BofA/GS trading revenue warnings

bullets.text: Kotak hosts TechM CEO Mohit Joshi & CFO Rohit Anand today 1400 IST on turnaround structural factors and AI-driven spending shifts.
bullets.source: Kotak - Reminder: Fireside chat with TechM leadership | Wed 23 Sep | 1400 IST

detail.summary: A closed-door, recorded fireside chat with Tech Mahindra's CEO and CFO covering the turnaround's structural underpinnings, enterprise-tech spending shifts toward AI, positioning for the AI wave, and financial discipline versus strategic investment.
points: Structural turnaround factors and path ahead
AI adoption shifting enterprise tech spending priorities

bullets.text: WPI–core CPI gap widened to 592bps (3-month avg), signaling margin pressure into 4QFY27; Ambit turns cautious on Transmission, SELL on Afcons.
bullets.source: Ambit - Sales: Consumer event; Cautious on transmission; Economy: WPI-core CPI gap widening

detail.summary: Ambit flags a widening WPI-core CPI gap (manufacturing components inflating above 4% rose from 28% to 61%) as a margin risk through 4QFY27 given Brent above $90. It turns cautious on transmission equipment (execution ~35% below target) and reiterates SELL on Afcons as metro price wars cap margins.
points: Transmission pecking order: GVTD>Hitachi>ENRIN>CG Power, all SELL
Afcons incumbent share down to 10-15% from 20%

bullets.text: Brent back above $100/bbl and INR down >1% in two weeks push India's 10Y yield past 7%, with FII selling resuming.
bullets.source: BNP Paribas - BNPP INDIA QUICK NOTES: CHINA Xi in the US | INDIA ECO CHARTBOOK | CORPORATE SURVEY - CAPEX maintained

detail.summary: BNP flags oil and a high base as headwinds, even as FX reserves near $800bn on FCNR inflows offer near-term cushion. Manufacturing PMI has fallen to its lowest since Aug-21.
points: Brent back above $100/bbl amid Middle East escalation

bullets.text: Small & midcap MF inflows hit record highs (Rs7,970cr/Rs6,990cr in Aug) as Large Cap funds see a 2nd straight month of outflows.
bullets.source: Elara - The Domestic Liquidity Tracker: domestic liquidity crowding into SMIDs (+2 more in Outlook)

detail.summary: Elara's tracker shows domestic flows rotating from Large Caps into SMIDs, both printing record monthly inflows in August. SMID funds are now ~50-55% of active equity inflows, but flow-adjusted investor returns lag reported NAV returns by wide margins.
points: Aug equity inflows Rs29,330cr, up from Rs24,700cr
Large Cap funds: 2nd straight month of outflows
Midcap NAV CAGR ~14% vs flow-adjusted investor return ~4%

bullets.text: BofA initiates Ather Energy at Buy, PO Rs1,900, citing EV adoption past its tipping point and 16% market share (top 3).
bullets.source: BofA - India Insight: Initiate on Ather Energy (Buy) & PhysicsWallah (Sell)

detail.summary: BofA frames Ather as the best proxy on India's 2-wheeler EV adoption, past the validation phase with 16% share and premium pricing; the next leg is scale via the EL platform and AURIC capacity (1.4m units) with demand ahead of supply, lifting EBITDA margin to low teens by FY31.
points: EBITDAm seen reaching low teens by FY31

ai_semis.text: SOX +2.06%, AMD +9.95% as the post-Meta Muse agentic-AI rally rotated into semis and memory; NDX hit a new high.
BNPP's Santa Clara checks with AMD, Nvidia, Broadcom show no AI-infra slowdown; memory/storage demand still exceeds supply.
ai_semis.source: BNP Paribas - India Quick Notes: SEMIs - No slowdown in AI Infra demand

ai_semis.text: TrendForce sees Q4 NAND pricing +20% QoQ on the AI-driven DRAM shortage; Samsung closing the HBM4 gap on SK Hynix.
ai_semis.source: BofA - ASIA Daily: APAC Conf Day 3
